title: まま: the unchanged condition
summary: まま is a noun meaning "an unchanged condition". Every use of it, from そのまま to わがまま, comes from that one idea.

blocks.text: Grammar lists give まま a pile of meanings ("as it is", "as one wishes", "a state") and even call it a particle. Use the word-type test from lesson 41 instead. まま does not end in an う-row kana and does not end in い, so it is a **noun**. Which noun? An **unchanged condition**. Whenever you see まま, read "unchanged condition".

Because まま is a noun, anything that describes it comes before it: another noun with **の**, an い-adjective, or a whole verb phrase. The word carries an extra hint: the condition could have changed, but it has not.

blocks.jp: 自然のままの森を歩いた。
blocks.en: (I) walked through a forest in its natural, untouched state.

blocks.jp: パジャマのまま朝ごはんを食べた。
blocks.en: (I) ate breakfast still in my pajamas.

blocks.jp: いつまでも若いままでいたい。
窓を開けたまま寝てしまった。
blocks.en: (I) fell asleep with the window left open.

blocks.text: 窓を開けたまま寝てしまった。The describer sits in front of the noun まま. (The で after まま has dropped.)

まま often takes the copula で ("being the unchanged condition"). Like a time expression it may drop that で. The meaning stays "while it stays in its unchanged condition". Picture someone holding out a dish of boiled soybeans:

lines.jp: そのままで食べられるの？
lines.en: Can you eat them just as they are?

lines.jp: うん、そのまま食べられるよ。
lines.en: Yes, you can eat them as they are.

blocks.text: In 思いのまま and 心のまま, the "unchanged condition" is a match with your own thoughts or heart. The world outside stays just as the inside wants it.

blocks.jp: 思いのままに動けない。

blocks.text: From the same idea comes **わがまま**: わが is "my", so it is "my own unchanged condition", a person who wants the world to follow their will. That is selfishness.

blocks.jp: わがままを言わないで。
blocks.en: Don't be selfish. (Don't say selfish things.)

items: まま is a **noun**: an **unchanged condition**.
The describing part goes before it: **Nのまま**, **い-adjective + まま**, **verb (た / ない) + まま**.
The で after it can drop: そのまま食べる.
**思いのまま** = as one wishes; **わがまま** = my own way, selfish.

questions.prompt: めがねをかけたまま寝てしまった。
options: I put on my glasses after sleeping
I fell asleep with my glasses still on
I slept and broke my glasses
I will sleep with my glasses on
questions.note: かけた + まま: the glasses stayed on.
questions.en: I fell asleep with my glasses still on.

questions.prompt: 電気をつけた＿＿、出かけてしまった。
questions.note: つけた + まま: an unchanged condition.
questions.en: I went out leaving the light on.

questions.prompt: コートを着た＿＿、部屋に入った。
questions.en: I entered the room still wearing my coat.
This town is just as it was long ago.

questions.prompt: 古いままの家に住んでいる。
questions.en: I live in a house that is still old.

questions.instruction: What does のまま mean here?
questions.prompt: 彼は昔のままで、少しも変わらない。
options: Exactly as he used to be
questions.en: He is just as he used to be; he has not changed at all.

questions.instruction: What does ないまま mean?
questions.prompt: くつをぬがないまま、家に入った。
options: While still not having taken them off
questions.note: Verb (ない) + まま: the undone condition stays.
questions.en: I went into the house without taking off my shoes.

questions.instruction: Which form comes right before まま?
questions.note: In this lesson's examples, まま follows the past form (or ない).
questions.en: I slept with the window open.

questions.instruction: What does わがまま mean?
questions.prompt: 彼はわがままで、人の意見を聞かない。
options: Selfish: wanting everything his own way
questions.note: わが = my; my own unchanged condition.
questions.en: He is selfish and does not listen to others' opinions.

questions.instruction: Which phrase means "just as it was long ago"?

options: パジャマのまま出かけた。
窓を開けたまま出かけた。
窓を開けるまま出かけた。
questions.note: Verb + まま needs た or ない.

questions.instruction: What does まま also hint?
options: It could have changed, but did not
questions.note: That hint is part of the word.

questions.instruction: What does このまま mean here?
questions.prompt: このまま行けば、間に合う。
options: Keeping things as they are now
questions.note: このまま: this unchanged condition.
questions.en: If we keep going like this, we will make it in time.

questions.instruction: Which sentence says "I ate it raw, as it was"?

questions.prompt: I fell asleep with the air conditioner on.
questions.en: I fell asleep with the air conditioner on.

questions.prompt: This town stays as it was.
questions.en: This town stays as it was.

questions.instruction: Tap the noun that means "unchanged condition"
questions.note: まま is the noun; はいた describes it.
questions.en: I came in with my shoes on.
I keep using it as it is, old.
He is selfish, which is a problem.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that means "as it is"
questions.note: そのまま: in its unchanged condition.
questions.en: Please eat it as it is.
